\begin{abstract}
We evaluate a policy adopted by 12 of 24 units of a synthetic panel in 2006 or 2010 with a staggered difference-in-differences design (Callaway--Sant'Anna group-time effects, never-adopters as the comparison group). The overall effect on the adopters is $-2.7616$ (standard error 0.2857). The pre-adoption effects are jointly indistinguishable from zero ($p = 0.9276$), a placebo with adoption moved three years earlier finds 0.0897, and the not-yet-adopted comparison group gives $-2.7814$.
\end{abstract}
